title: Ampere Force Direction
description: Essential: The response must correctly state that the Ampere force on the rod is vertically downward.

title: Final Mass Value
description: Essential: The response must provide the correct final mass of the rod as 0.01 kg (or equivalent).

title: Initial Force Balance
description: Important: The solution must apply Hooke's law and equilibrium to relate the initial spring elongation to the rod's weight (2kΔl₁ = mg).

title: Current Calculation
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply Ohm's law (I = E/R) to find the current in the circuit.

title: Ampere Force Magnitude
description: Important: The solution must correctly calculate the Ampere force using F = BIL with the rod's length, field, and current.

title: Final Force Balance
description: Important: The solution must set up the final equilibrium condition relating spring force, weight, and Ampere force (2k(Δl₁+Δl₂) = mg + F).

title: Systematic Equation Solving
description: Optional: The solution clearly eliminates the spring constant k to solve for the mass, showing logical algebraic steps.

title: Unit Consistency
description: Optional: The solution demonstrates consistent unit conversion (e.g., cm to m) throughout the calculation.

title: Sign/Force Direction Error
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly stating the Ampere force direction (e.g., upward) or misapplying the left-hand rule.

title: Spring Force Misapplication
description: Pitfall: Failing to account for both springs in the force balance (using kΔl instead of 2kΔl) or misinterpreting the elongation change.
